atlas.statement: Stagflation-tinged tightening: a Fed preparing to hike into a 5% ten-year and 2.88% real yields permits only quality ballast and a lot of cash. Because real rates set the discount on every long-duration story, a beat-and-raise from NVDA could not lift it. With HY spreads 77bp wider in three months and the VIX at 30, I would not buy that dip. Our own stops say the same: TSM, MU, NVDA, ETN, ADI and AMD all breached their stated rotate levels, and WTI under $85 triggers the energy exits. I keep MSFT and a little ANET as the future we still own. My bias is to be early, so here is what would change my call: a soft PCE on Nov 25 plus HY back under 3.2pp. Then we redeploy.

Part 2. CB and PGR lose the float story, and CB's own 10y<4.5% rule fires. KO, WMT and MCK de-rate 15-20%. A drug-pricing bill hits LLY, ABBV and JNJ together. 28% cash and no growth beta: the book falls while SPY recovers.

The core assumption was wrong: we treated low beta as low risk. Measured: our holdings are about 40% one crowded factor, roughly 0.9 correlated in an unwind. Correlation, not volatility, sets the drawdown.

My fix: healthcare capped at 10% and insurers at 7.5%. MCK dropped, KO and WMT cut. An 18% growth sleeve of relative-strength leaders with positive beta: AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, ANET, PANW, CRWD, DIS. Every holding has a written stop.
Your rebound thesis informs the hedge, not the entry. I add beta through names already above their 200-day, never through knives. If SMH reclaims its 50-day, that is my signal to add semis.

forge.statement: The pre-mortem that kills us is not an AI crash. It is AI capex discipline. A hyperscaler trims 2027 capex, so the spenders rally on free cash flow while the suppliers fall. Inflation cools after one hike, and money rotates out of our crowded low-beta refuge. We would hold the supplier side through ANET, and 11% in pharma exposed to one drug-pricing bill. We would own none of the spender upside and only a thin slice of the index. So I trim ANET to 3.5% and ABBV to 2%. I add AMZN at 2.5%, which pays a 6.1% FCF yield, so a capex cut helps it rather than hurts it. RSP at 4% means we are not shut out if the S&P rises. Cash falls to 47%.

scout:
**THE FUTURE: Scout dispatch, Fri 20 Nov 2026, about 16:00 GMT (11:00 ET)**

**Lead: the AI trade is breaking, and the Fed is hiking, not cutting.**

**1. Last 7 days**

- **Nvidia (NVDA).**
  - Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on Nov 12 after reports of extramarital affairs. 
CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO.
 
The board chair said on the earnings call that Huang will not return.
 
The SEC is reportedly investigating
, and 
California's attorney general has issued a subpoena.

  - It beat on Nov 17. 
Q3 revenue was $115.84B against $109.10B expected, and Q4 guidance was $130B against $125.1B.
 The stock fell anyway. 
It is on track for its longest weekly losing streak since 2008.
 
It traded near $141.56 this morning, below every close since June 5, 2025.

  - A beat-and-raise that can't lift the stock is the signal to watch.
- **Chips and AI broadly.**
  - 
A short-seller report alleging export-control violations hit AMD on Thursday
, and 
Nvidia faces similar allegations of chips funneled to China.
 AMD fell about 7.7% Thursday.
  - Friday morning: 
MU -5.4%, AVGO -4.3%, ASE -6%.
 
TSMC dropped 4.5%, and Taiwan stocks are heading for their worst weekly drop in nearly three decades.

  - 
Semiconductors are down more than 25% since early October.

- **Anthropic IPO.**
  - It is the largest IPO ever. 
It priced at $83, with 980m shares and $81.3bn raised.
 
It jumped 17% on its Nasdaq debut Thursday
, then 
pulled back Friday.

  - It did not revive AI sentiment. Neoclouds and data-centre names (IREN, Applied Digital, Core Scientific) fell about 7%.
- **Indexes.**
  - 
The Nasdaq turned negative for 2026 on Thursday.
 
The Dow is down roughly 6% for the week, its worst since April 2025.

  - Intraday Friday, 
the Nasdaq was down about 2.8% and the S&P 500 down about 1.6% at one point.
 Intraday numbers are conflicting, so treat them as unconfirmed until the close.
- **The Fed turned hawkish.**
  - 
Minutes of the October meeting said almost all participants saw further hikes as likely appropriate.
 
The October hold was 10–2, with Cook and Hammack dissenting for a hike.

  - 
Waller says the FOMC should consider a half-point hike in December.
 
The minutes also flag AI debt as a financial-stability risk.

  - 
September PCE was 3.6% headline and 3.1% core.
 
October CPI rose 0.4%.

  - Pricing: 
about a 99% chance of a December hike
 by one count. Another source had 
about 91% for 25bp and 9% for 50bp.
 The size of the hike is the open question.
- **Rates, commodities, crypto (Thursday snapshot).**
  - 
The 10-year Treasury yield was 5.08%, the VIX 22.6, gold $3,715, WTI $83.37 and Bitcoin about $63,600.

- **Winners.**
  - **PANW** beat. 
Revenue rose 39% to $3.44B, FY27 guidance was raised, and it is buying Applied Compute for $4.5B in stock.
 
The stock rose about 6% Thursday.
 
CRWD opened more than 6% higher in sympathy.
 That is a good read-through into CRWD's Dec 1 report.
  - **TJX** 
closed up 8.05%
 and raised guidance. Target and Lowe's earnings were 
flattered by tariff refunds.
 Quality of earnings is a caveat on retail.
  - **WMT** beat on Thursday. 
The stock was down about 1% at $126.04.

- **Other.**
  - 
Intel is cutting more jobs.

  - 
A US aviation shutdown has an unknown root cause.
 I could not confirm the scope. This matters for BA, AIR.PA, UBER and BKNG.
  - 
The Wednesday close had the Dow -1.1%, S&P -0.2% and Nasdaq +0.4%.


**2. Next two weeks**

Dates are as supplied. I did not re-verify them.

- **Mon–Tue Nov 23–24.** DELL reports Tuesday after the close, with ADI, MDT and BHP also due. DELL is the AI-server demand read after Nvidia's guide. Watch for AI-server backlog and margin commentary.
- **Wed Nov 25.** GDP and PCE. The supplied consensus is 3.4% GDP and 0.3% PCE. I could not confirm those numbers, and I don't know the PCE definition (monthly or core). With the Fed already leaning to a hike, a hot PCE print raises the odds of 50bp. DE reports before the open.
- **Thu Nov 26.** Markets closed for Thanksgiving. Expect a thin, shortened session Friday Nov 27. A weak tape plus thin liquidity can overshoot.
- **Tue Dec 1.** ISM manufacturing. CRWD and MRVL report after the close. MRVL is a direct AI-chip sentiment test.
- **Wed Dec 2.** BMO and BNS report before the open, and CRM after the close.
- **Thu Dec 3.** ISM services. RY and TD report before the open.
- **Fri Dec 4.** Jobs report. It is the last big labour print before the Fed.
- **Wed Dec 9.** FOMC decision, with new projections. 
Minutes said a hike larger than 25bp could be considered if inflation data are unfavorable.
 AVGO reports after the close, and it is already down about 4% today.
- **Thu Dec 10.** CPI. COST reports after the close.
- **Unconfirmed.** I did not find confirmation of the Nvidia permanent-CEO timeline, other central bank meetings (ECB, BoJ), or index rebalancing dates in this window.

**3. Sentiment and positioning**

- 
Fund managers are reportedly dumping tech stocks at the fastest pace since 2006.
 I could not confirm the underlying survey.
- 
One earnings-mood gauge stood at 4/10 (cautious) as of Nov 13.
 Good news is being sold across chips.
- 
One fund manager called Nvidia "uninvestable"
, and 
nine houses downgraded it.
 Contrarians will note that this is capitulation-like language. One note says 
a sharp AI rebound is possible if inflation cools.

- Rotation is visible. The Dow and defensives held up Friday while tech sold off. Cybersecurity and off-price retail are the pockets being bought.

**What the council should hold in mind**

The future the council wants to hold is still AI compute. Nvidia's demand numbers are accelerating, with revenue up 103% year on year and Rubin shipping. What is breaking is the price, driven by three things: leadership and legal risk at Nvidia, a 5%+ 10-year yield with a Fed that wants to hike, and AI-debt worries. The three things to watch are the Nov 25 PCE print, DELL on Nov 24, and the Dec 9 FOMC size and dot plot. Quality AI-adjacent names with real earnings, such as PANW, showed buyers still exist.

redteam.statement: Roughly 21% of this book is one trade: insurers plus pharma near their highs, owned by eight of eight seats. CB, BRK-B, PGR, LLY, JNJ and ABBV are not diversified ballast. Pulse measured that factor at about 0.9 correlation in an unwind. The hedge against it is IEF at 1.3%, which is a gesture, not a hedge. Meanwhile 'The Future' holds about 15% in AI. Its anchor, ANET, sits 1.3% above the stop that DELL can trip on Tuesday. The spender-versus-supplier hedge failed this week: MSFT fell 5.5% while ANET fell 13.5%. Part of the plan is sound. Exit the fired-stop names, especially ADI before its Monday pre-market print, and keep 42% cash. Then fix the cluster or name it as the bet.

attacks.argument: CB 4.4, BRK-B 4.0, PGR 2.9, LLY 3.7, JNJ 3.0 and ABBV 2.1 come to about 20% of capital, or 35% of invested. All are near highs with unanimous ownership. A soft PCE on Nov 25 empties the refuge together, and the 1.3% IEF cannot offset it.

At 174x P/E, the 44% operating margin against a 10% net margin is unexplained, a footnote no seat has read. Beta is 2.44 and the stock is 1.3% above its 200-day exit. A DELL Nov 24 or MRVL Dec 1 wobble likely forces a sale at the low.

The spender-versus-supplier hedge is a story, not a measurement. This week MSFT fell 5.5%, AMZN 4.7% and ANET 13.5%, all in the same direction. In a financing-driven de-rating, spenders and suppliers fall together. AI exposure is effectively one factor at about 15%.

October earnings fell year on year on rising expenses, and latest-quarter growth is 3%, down 4.3pp. It duplicates CB's float factor, and CB's own latest-quarter growth is 0.3%. Two insurers with decelerating top lines at their highs is a softening pricing cycle that the price has not yet reflected.

MSFT is the largest weight but sits 5% below its 50-day, with an executive-change 8-K on Nov 5 and Anthropic-linked spending commitments. The 1.6% FCF yield sits below a 5% Treasury. Its cushion to the $444 stop is about 10%, which is fine, but it is the book's single-largest beta-1 name.

Growth decelerated 9.1pp, the stock fell 6% this week, and it is the top XLV holding being sold by ETFs. At 46x earnings and 21% above its 200-day, any drug-pricing headline from the new Congress reprices it and drags JNJ and ABBV with it.
The paper book still holds 2.9% ADI, 8.8% below its 50-day, so its stop has fired. It reports Nov 24 pre-market. The consensus drops it, but only Monday's session is left to execute before the print.

cut.reason: At 0.8%, 28.7x after a 41% run, it is the purest crowded refuge. The council itself calls it the first to empty on a pivot.
At 0.6% it is token size. It adds to the same low-vol factor and incurs costs without changing the risk.
Earnings are declining, growth is 3%, and it duplicates CB's float factor. It is a fourth seat in a crowded cluster.

blind_spots: The data feed is unreliable in places. V shows an 8.1x P/E and a $191B cap, MA a $77.7B cap and IBKR a $3.1B cap. Seats cite these sheets without verifying them.
The 10-year in the cross-asset table is 4.94 against 5.07 from FRED. Exits keyed to 5.2% or 4.5% need one agreed source.
Token positions (NVDA 0.6, RO.SW 0.6, MO 0.6) are neither hedge nor bet; they cost about 0.2% round-trip for no effect on outcomes.
The awareness says to hold the future, but the book holds more in insurers than in AI suppliers. If AI demand is accelerating, the council is underweight its own mandate by choice.
redteam.killer_scenario: Core PCE prints 0.2% on Nov 25 and Dec 9 delivers a 'last' 25bp hike. Rotation dumps insurers and pharma 6-10% while semis squeeze 20%+. The book, with about 20% in the refuge cluster and 0.6% NVDA, lags by 5-8 points in three weeks.

risk.statement: Largest risk: about 20% of capital is one refuge trade, with insurers, pharma and BRK-B at roughly 0.9 correlation. The limit is per-name caps that hold CB, BRK-B, LLY, JNJ and ABBV to 17% combined, paired with real duration, IEF of 3% or more. Second risk: AI trades as one factor at beta 2-plus in front of DELL, MRVL, CRWD and AVGO prints. I cap ANET, PANW, CRWD and NVDA. Third: binaries that coincide with stops already fired. ADI is out by Monday's close, and no seat argues otherwise. AVGO reports on FOMC night, so it is vetoed. With VIX at 30 and hikes priced, minimum cash is 30%. No sector above 20%. I do not veto NVDA; its governance risk is handled by size.

vetoes.reason: Stop fired at 8.8% below its 50-day, and it reports Nov 24 pre-market. Exit Monday; holding through the print is an unhedged binary.
Reports Dec 9 after the close, the same day as the FOMC. A stacked binary at beta 2.25, 14% below its 200-day.
0.6x P/E and a 149.9% FCF yield look like a data artifact. Volatility 94%, beta 3.94, down 48% in a month.
-9.1% FCF yield funding a $664B backlog, beta 2.25. The AI-debt financing risk the Fed minutes flagged.
Prints Nov 24 with growth decelerating 30pp, beta 2.63, 88% volatility. A pure binary in a broken trend.
Trades below its IPO price, AI-chip debt priced above 8% yield, FAA and Congressional scrutiny, beta 2.48.

concerns: The refuge cluster (CB, BRK-B, LLY, JNJ, ABBV) unwinds together on a soft Nov 25 PCE. Keep IEF at 3% or more as the offset.
AI exposure (MSFT, AMZN, ANET, PANW, GOOG, NVDA) is one financing factor. Hold it at about 16% or less in total, and enforce the 200-day stops mechanically after DELL on Nov 24 and MRVL on Dec 1.
Event stack: PCE Nov 25, payrolls Dec 4, FOMC Dec 9 (a 50bp hike is possible), CPI Dec 10. Redeploy cash after the prints, not before them.
Data integrity: ANET's 44% operating versus 10% net margin gap, COF's 104% net margin and IBKR's market cap are unverified. Do not size any of them on those figures.
Thin Thanksgiving liquidity on Nov 27, with VIX at 30, can overshoot stops. Prefer executing on full sessions.

chairRaw.statement: The council will hold 54% invested and 46% cash. The book gets a real duration hedge, a capped refuge and a named AI bet. Three arguments carried this. First, Vex measured the refuge at roughly 0.9 correlation, so CB, BRK-B, LLY, JNJ and ABBV are capped at 14.5% and offset by 4.5% IEF. Second, spender and supplier fell together this week, so AI is one factor of about 15%, and every name in it has a mechanical stop. Third, stops that fired are executed. ADI, ETN, TSM, AMD and MU go on Monday, as do the oil hedges, because WTI broke $85. I keep NVDA at 1% as the cheap side of a semis squeeze, re-underwritten with a new stop. I overrule the seats who would sell it on the old one. We redeploy after PCE, payrolls and the FOMC, not before.

events.text:
**THE FUTURE: Scout dispatch, Fri 20 Nov 2026, about 16:00 GMT (11:00 ET)**

**Lead: the AI trade is breaking, and the Fed is hiking, not cutting.**

**1. Last 7 days**

- **Nvidia (NVDA).**
  - Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on Nov 12 after reports of extramarital affairs. 
CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO.
 
The board chair said on the earnings call that Huang will not return.
 
The SEC is reportedly investigating
, and 
California's attorney general has issued a subpoena.

  - It beat on Nov 17. 
Q3 revenue was $115.84B against $109.10B expected, and Q4 guidance was $130B against $125.1B.
 The stock fell anyway. 
It is on track for its longest weekly losing streak since 2008.
 
It traded near $141.56 this morning, below every close since June 5, 2025.

  - A beat-and-raise that can't lift the stock is the signal to watch.
- **Chips and AI broadly.**
  - 
A short-seller report alleging export-control violations hit AMD on Thursday
, and 
Nvidia faces similar allegations of chips funneled to China.
 AMD fell about 7.7% Thursday.
  - Friday morning: 
MU -5.4%, AVGO -4.3%, ASE -6%.
 
TSMC dropped 4.5%, and Taiwan stocks are heading for their worst weekly drop in nearly three decades.

  - 
Semiconductors are down more than 25% since early October.

- **Anthropic IPO.**
  - It is the largest IPO ever. 
It priced at $83, with 980m shares and $81.3bn raised.
 
It jumped 17% on its Nasdaq debut Thursday
, then 
pulled back Friday.

  - It did not revive AI sentiment. Neoclouds and data-centre names (IREN, Applied Digital, Core Scientific) fell about 7%.
- **Indexes.**
  - 
The Nasdaq turned negative for 2026 on Thursday.
 
The Dow is down roughly 6% for the week, its worst since April 2025.

  - Intraday Friday, 
the Nasdaq was down about 2.8% and the S&P 500 down about 1.6% at one point.
 Intraday numbers are conflicting, so treat them as unconfirmed until the close.
- **The Fed turned hawkish.**
  - 
Minutes of the October meeting said almost all participants saw further hikes as likely appropriate.
 
The October hold was 10–2, with Cook and Hammack dissenting for a hike.

  - 
Waller says the FOMC should consider a half-point hike in December.
 
The minutes also flag AI debt as a financial-stability risk.

  - 
September PCE was 3.6% headline and 3.1% core.
 
October CPI rose 0.4%.

  - Pricing: 
about a 99% chance of a December hike
 by one count. Another source had 
about 91% for 25bp and 9% for 50bp.
 The size of the hike is the open question.
- **Rates, commodities, crypto (Thursday snapshot).**
  - 
The 10-year Treasury yield was 5.08%, the VIX 22.6, gold $3,715, WTI $83.37 and Bitcoin about $63,600.

- **Winners.**
  - **PANW** beat. 
Revenue rose 39% to $3.44B, FY27 guidance was raised, and it is buying Applied Compute for $4.5B in stock.
 
The stock rose about 6% Thursday.
 
CRWD opened more than 6% higher in sympathy.
 That is a good read-through into CRWD's Dec 1 report.
  - **TJX** 
closed up 8.05%
 and raised guidance. Target and Lowe's earnings were 
flattered by tariff refunds.
 Quality of earnings is a caveat on retail.
  - **WMT** beat on Thursday. 
The stock was down about 1% at $126.04.

- **Other.**
  - 
Intel is cutting more jobs.

  - 
A US aviation shutdown has an unknown root cause.
 I could not confirm the scope. This matters for BA, AIR.PA, UBER and BKNG.
  - 
The Wednesday close had the Dow -1.1%, S&P -0.2% and Nasdaq +0.4%.


**2. Next two weeks**

Dates are as supplied. I did not re-verify them.

- **Mon–Tue Nov 23–24.** DELL reports Tuesday after the close, with ADI, MDT and BHP also due. DELL is the AI-server demand read after Nvidia's guide. Watch for AI-server backlog and margin commentary.
- **Wed Nov 25.** GDP and PCE. The supplied consensus is 3.4% GDP and 0.3% PCE. I could not confirm those numbers, and I don't know the PCE definition (monthly or core). With the Fed already leaning to a hike, a hot PCE print raises the odds of 50bp. DE reports before the open.
- **Thu Nov 26.** Markets closed for Thanksgiving. Expect a thin, shortened session Friday Nov 27. A weak tape plus thin liquidity can overshoot.
- **Tue Dec 1.** ISM manufacturing. CRWD and MRVL report after the close. MRVL is a direct AI-chip sentiment test.
- **Wed Dec 2.** BMO and BNS report before the open, and CRM after the close.
- **Thu Dec 3.** ISM services. RY and TD report before the open.
- **Fri Dec 4.** Jobs report. It is the last big labour print before the Fed.
- **Wed Dec 9.** FOMC decision, with new projections. 
Minutes said a hike larger than 25bp could be considered if inflation data are unfavorable.
 AVGO reports after the close, and it is already down about 4% today.
- **Thu Dec 10.** CPI. COST reports after the close.
- **Unconfirmed.** I did not find confirmation of the Nvidia permanent-CEO timeline, other central bank meetings (ECB, BoJ), or index rebalancing dates in this window.

**3. Sentiment and positioning**

- 
Fund managers are reportedly dumping tech stocks at the fastest pace since 2006.
 I could not confirm the underlying survey.
- 
One earnings-mood gauge stood at 4/10 (cautious) as of Nov 13.
 Good news is being sold across chips.
- 
One fund manager called Nvidia "uninvestable"
, and 
nine houses downgraded it.
 Contrarians will note that this is capitulation-like language. One note says 
a sharp AI rebound is possible if inflation cools.

- Rotation is visible. The Dow and defensives held up Friday while tech sold off. Cybersecurity and off-price retail are the pockets being bought.

**What the council should hold in mind**

The future the council wants to hold is still AI compute. Nvidia's demand numbers are accelerating, with revenue up 103% year on year and Rubin shipping. What is breaking is the price, driven by three things: leadership and legal risk at Nvidia, a 5%+ 10-year yield with a Fed that wants to hike, and AI-debt worries. The three things to watch are the Nov 25 PCE print, DELL on Nov 24, and the Dec 9 FOMC size and dot plot. Quality AI-adjacent names with real earnings, such as PANW, showed buyers still exist.

data.statement: Stagflation-tinged tightening: a Fed preparing to hike into a 5% ten-year and 2.88% real yields permits only quality ballast and a lot of cash. Because real rates set the discount on every long-duration story, a beat-and-raise from NVDA could not lift it. With HY spreads 77bp wider in three months and the VIX at 30, I would not buy that dip. Our own stops say the same: TSM, MU, NVDA, ETN, ADI and AMD all breached their stated rotate levels, and WTI under $85 triggers the energy exits. I keep MSFT and a little ANET as the future we still own. My bias is to be early, so here is what would change my call: a soft PCE on Nov 25 plus HY back under 3.2pp. Then we redeploy.
